newsitem.title: USA: Cuba dispute ties up U.S. House for hours.
newsitem.headline: Cuba dispute ties up U.S. House for hours.

text.p: A dispute over a small amendment involving Cuba led the U.S. House of Representatives to tie itself up for hours Wednesday casting a second set of votes on 23 foreign policy measures it had already settled.
Except for the Cuba amendment, which was defeated, all the other votes turned out the same way as the first go-round.

Representative Jose Serrano, a New York Democrat, had won passage of the Cuba amendment earlier this month. It would have required the State Department to tell Congress about any complaints Cuba lodged with U.S. agencies about activities of U.S. residents, such as the exiles based in Miami.

When foes of that amendment, including Florida lawmakers with fierce opposition to Cuban President Fidel Castro, found that the amendment had passed and not enough of them had been present to block it, they demanded that it be reconsidered.
In response, an angry Serrano invoked a procedural rule that let him demand time-consuming recorded votes on 22 other foreign policy amendments that had already passed in swifter voice votes.
"On this I ask for a recorded vote," Serrano declared more than 20 times as each amendment came up in an exercise that occupied the House for several hours.

"If they want to vote again on an amendment because they weren't there (the first time), he felt other members should have an opportunity to vote again on amendments that they were not there for," said Serrano spokeswoman Ivonne Cunarro.
Serrano said the amendment would ensure Congress is informed of Cuban complaints about violations of Cuban airspace, dropping of anti-Castro flyers, and similar actions.

He has said the amendment would "provide the U.S. Congress with vital information that could prevent tragedies such as the shooting down of the two planes piloted by members of Brothers to the Rescue last year."
But his critics said it was outrageous to have U.S. agencies investigating its own citizens or residents because Castro complained.
